title: Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis

methods.one_paragraph_description: Diffuser is a denoising diffusion model over two-dimensional trajectory arrays (states and actions over the planning horizon). At runtime it observes the current state, initializes a plan from Gaussian noise, and iteratively denoises it for N steps; at each reverse step the mean is shifted by the gradient of a separately trained return predictor J_phi (classifier-style guidance, scale alpha), and the first state of the plan is constrained to the observed state via inpainting. The first action of the sampled plan is executed and the procedure repeats in a receding-horizon control loop (Algorithm 1).
methods.conventional_lineage_hint: model-based reinforcement learning / diffusion-based planning: 'Model-based reinforcement learning methods often use learning only for the purpose of estimating an approximate dynamics model' ... 'we propose to fold as much of the trajectory optimization pipeline as possible into the modeling problem' ; evaluated on 'the D4RL offline locomotion suite' (Section 5.3 Offline Reinforcement Learning)

return_predictor_architecture.value: first half of the U-Net + final linear layer
return_predictor_architecture.quote: The return predictor J has the structure of the first half of the U-Net used for the diffusion model, with a final linear layer to produce a scalar output.

planning_horizon.quote: We use a planning horizon T of 32 in all locomotion tasks, 128 for block-stacking, 128 in Maze2D / Multi2D U-Maze, 265 in Maze2D / Multi2D Medium, and 384 in Maze2D / Multi2D Large.

diffusion_steps.quote: We use N = 20 diffusion steps for locomotion tasks and N = 100 for block-stacking.

guide_scale.quote: We use a guide scale of α = 0.1 for all tasks except hopper-medium-expert, in which we use a smaller scale of 0.0001.

discount.quote: We used a discount factor of 0.997 for the return prediction Jφ , though found that above γ = 0.99 planning was fairly insensitive to changes in discount factor.

horizon_reduction_note.value: horizon can be reduced with lower guide scale, e.g. 0.001 for horizon 4 on halfcheetah (no results table given)
horizon_reduction_note.quote: We found that we could reduce the planning horizon for many tasks, but that the guide scale would need to be lowered (e.g., to 0.001 for a horizon of 4 in the halfcheetah tasks) to accommodate.
